chunks.title: The for statement
chunks.text: The for statement has three parts: initialization, termination condition and increment. for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) runs the body n times. The enhanced for-each (for (Type item : collection)) iterates over arrays and Iterables.
chunks.nudge: Think about your loop bounds: does the condition use < or <=, and does it cover every index you need?

chunks.title: The while statement
chunks.text: while (condition) repeats the body as long as condition is true. do-while runs the body at least once, then checks the condition. Make sure something inside the loop changes the condition.
chunks.nudge: Check what changes each iteration so the loop eventually terminates.

chunks.title: The if-then-else statement
chunks.text: if (condition) runs a block when the condition is true. else if adds more branches. else is the fallback. Only one branch executes. Conditions must be boolean expressions (no truthy/falsy like in JavaScript).
chunks.nudge: Make sure your condition evaluates to a boolean. If you need to compare objects, use .equals() instead of ==.

chunks.title: Equality and relational operators
chunks.text: Relational: <, >, <=, >=. Equality: == (reference/value for primitives), != (not equal). For objects, == checks reference identity; use .equals() for value equality. String comparison always needs .equals(), never ==.
chunks.nudge: If comparing Strings or objects, use .equals() — the == operator compares references, not contents.

chunks.title: Arithmetic operators
chunks.text: Java supports +, -, *, / and % (remainder). Integer division truncates: 7/2 gives 3. To get a floating-point result, cast one operand: (double)a / b. No power operator; use Math.pow(base, exp) which returns double.
chunks.nudge: If dividing two ints gives an unexpected result, remember Java integer division truncates toward zero.

chunks.title: Math class
chunks.text: Math provides static methods: Math.abs(), Math.max(), Math.min(), Math.pow(a, b), Math.sqrt(), Math.floor(), Math.ceil(), Math.round(), Math.random(). Math.pow returns double; cast to int or long if needed.
chunks.nudge: Need a power or absolute value? Check the Math class. Remember Math.pow returns a double.

chunks.title: Defining methods
chunks.text: Methods are declared with a return type, name and parameter list: public int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; }. void methods don't return a value. Every non-void method must return on all code paths. Methods can be overloaded (same name, different parameters).
chunks.nudge: Make sure every branch of your method reaches a return statement with the correct type.

chunks.title: The return statement
chunks.text: return exits the method and provides the value to the caller. The value's type must match the method's declared return type. A void method can use return; with no value to exit early.
chunks.nudge: If you get a 'missing return statement' error, check that all if/else branches return a value.

chunks.title: Primitive data types
chunks.text: Java has 8 primitives: byte, short, int, long, float, double, boolean, char. int is 32-bit (±2 billion). long is 64-bit. float/double for decimals. Wrapper classes (Integer, Double) for object contexts. Auto-boxing converts between them.
chunks.nudge: If your numbers overflow or you get precision issues, check whether int is large enough or if you need long or double.

chunks.title: Strings
chunks.text: Strings are immutable objects. Common methods: .length(), .charAt(i), .substring(start, end), .indexOf(str), .contains(str), .equals(str), .equalsIgnoreCase(str), .toUpperCase(), .toLowerCase(), .trim(), .split(regex), .replace(old, new). Use StringBuilder for efficient concatenation in loops.
chunks.nudge: Remember Strings are immutable. Each method returns a new String; use StringBuilder if building in a loop.

chunks.title: Arrays
chunks.text: Arrays have fixed size: int[] arr = new int[n] or int[] arr = {1, 2, 3}. Access by index (0-based), .length gives the size (no parentheses). ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on invalid index. Use Arrays.sort(), Arrays.copyOf(), Arrays.toString() from java.util.Arrays.
chunks.nudge: Array length is a field (.length), not a method. Check your indices stay within 0 to length-1.

chunks.title: ArrayList
chunks.text: ArrayList<E> is a resizable array: .add(e), .get(i), .set(i, e), .remove(i), .size(), .contains(e), .indexOf(e). Cannot hold primitives directly; use wrapper types (Integer, Double). Iterate with for-each or indices.
chunks.nudge: If you need a growable list, use ArrayList. Remember it uses wrapper types, not primitives.

chunks.title: HashMap
chunks.text: HashMap<K,V> stores key-value pairs: .put(k, v), .get(k), .containsKey(k), .remove(k), .size(), .keySet(), .values(), .entrySet(). get returns null for missing keys; use getOrDefault(k, default) to avoid NullPointerException.
chunks.nudge: If you need to look up values by key, use a HashMap. Check for null returns from .get() when the key might be absent.

chunks.title: try-catch-finally
chunks.text: try { ... } catch (ExceptionType e) { ... } catches specific exception types. finally always runs. Checked exceptions must be caught or declared with throws. Common: NullPointerException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, NumberFormatException, IOException.
chunks.nudge: If the compiler says you must handle an exception, wrap the risky code in try/catch with the specific exception type.

chunks.title: null in Java
chunks.text: null means no object reference. Calling a method on null throws NullPointerException. Check with if (obj != null) before use. Primitives cannot be null, but their wrapper types (Integer, etc.) can be.
chunks.nudge: If you get NullPointerException, trace which variable is null and add a null check before using it.

chunks.title: Collections.sort()
chunks.text: Collections.sort(list) sorts a List in natural order. For custom order: Collections.sort(list, comparator) or list.sort(comparator). Comparator.comparingInt(fn) sorts by an int key. Arrays.sort(arr) sorts an array in place.
chunks.nudge: Use Collections.sort() for Lists and Arrays.sort() for arrays. Provide a Comparator for custom order.

chunks.title: Boolean operators
chunks.text: && is logical AND (short-circuit), || is logical OR (short-circuit), ! is logical NOT. Short-circuit means the second operand is not evaluated if the first determines the result. Use parentheses to clarify complex conditions.
chunks.nudge: If your condition is complex, break it into parts and check the truth table. && short-circuits on false, || on true.

chunks.title: Integer.parseInt()
chunks.text: Integer.parseInt(str) converts a String to int. Throws NumberFormatException for invalid input. Double.parseDouble(str) for doubles. String.valueOf(n) converts a number to String.
chunks.nudge: If converting a String to a number, be ready for NumberFormatException on non-numeric input.
